Interface SdCard

All Known Implementing Classes:
NativeSdCard
public interface SdCard
Access to an SPI SD card, backed by the Arduino SdFat library with long-file-name support enabled.

Take the card from the shield or carrier that holds its socket, once, at startup: DataLoggerShield.getSdCard(), TftTouchShield.getSdCard(), LcdKeypadShield.getSdCard(), ArduinoWifiShield.getSdCard() or NanoConnectorCarrier.getSdCard(), or from M5StackCardputer.getSd() for the Cardputer's built-in socket. A unit test passes mock(SdCard.class) instead.

Call begin() for the chip-select pin of the socket the card came from, or begin(int) for custom wiring, before opening or writing files. A root-level path uses the SD card's root as its base and must be a compile-time string literal. The folder-aware overloads accept runtime directory and file-stem strings; they are intended for bounded dynamic layouts such as /mailbox/YYYYMMDD/<uuid>.txt. open(String) is read-only; the writers, appendLine(String, String) (adds a line) and appendText(String, String) (adds raw text), each open the file, write, and close it again rather than keeping a writable handle open. To replace a file, remove(String) it first.

Limits:

  • Root-level paths are compile-time string literals, so their length is not limited by the runtime. Folder-aware directory and file-stem strings each fit in a runtime string slot; the native SD layer combines them.
  • A literal line passed to appendLine(String, String) has no length limit either, but a line built while the program runs (String.valueOf, concatenation, StringBuilder.toString()) lives in a runtime-string slot of io.github.jabrena.juno.RuntimeLimits#STRING_SLOT_CAPACITY_BYTES bytes including the NUL terminator: 31 characters at most, and a longer value panics rather than truncating. Split longer records over several calls; each call ends its line with a newline.

  • Method Details

    • begin

      boolean begin()
      Initializes the card on the chip-select pin of the socket it came from (D10 on the data logger and TFT shields, D4 on the Arduino WiFi Shield and the Nano Connector Carrier, or GPIO12 on the Cardputer) and returns whether it was detected successfully.

    • begin

      boolean begin(int chipSelectPin)
      Initializes the card on chipSelectPin and returns whether it was detected successfully.

    • exists

      boolean exists(String path)
      Returns whether path exists on the card.

    • createDirectory

      boolean createDirectory(String path)
      Creates path and its missing parent directories. Returns whether the operation succeeded.

    • size

      int size(String path)
      Returns the size of path in bytes, or -1 when it does not exist or cannot be opened. A file over Integer.MAX_VALUE bytes reports Integer.MAX_VALUE. Use it to tell whether a log has grown too large or a file is empty; InputStream.available() only says whether bytes remain.

    • open

      InputStream open(String path)
      Opens path for reading, or returns null when it cannot be opened.

    • open

      InputStream open(String directory, String fileStem)
      Opens directory/fileStem.txt for reading, or returns null when it cannot be opened.

    • list

      int list(String directory, int index, byte[] name, int capacity)
      Copies the name of the direct child at index in directory into name. Returns the number of bytes copied, zero when there are no more children, or a negative value when the directory cannot be read or the buffer is too small.

    • appendLine

      boolean appendLine(String path, String line)
      Appends line plus a newline to path, creating the file first if it does not exist yet. Unlike open(), line may be a runtime string. Returns whether the write succeeded.

    • writeBytes

      boolean writeBytes(String path, byte[] data, int length)
      Creates or replaces path with the first length bytes of data, and returns whether the write succeeded. Use it for binary files such as JPEG frames; path is a compile-time string literal.

    • appendText

      boolean appendText(String path, String text)
      Appends text to path exactly as given, creating the file first if it does not exist yet: unlike appendLine(String, String) no newline is added, so a record can be written in pieces (each piece within the runtime-string limit above) or be raw text such as CSV fields. Returns whether the write succeeded.

    • appendText

      boolean appendText(String directory, String fileStem, String text)
      Appends text to directory/fileStem.txt, creating the file when needed.

    • remove

      boolean remove(String path)
      Deletes path from the card. Returns whether it was removed.

    • removeDirectory

      boolean removeDirectory(String path)
      Deletes the empty directory at path. Returns false when it is missing, non-empty, or cannot be removed.

    • remove

      boolean remove(String directory, String fileStem)
      Deletes directory/fileStem.txt from the card. Returns whether it was removed.

    • totalKiB

      int totalKiB()
      The card volume's total capacity in KiB, or -1 before a successful begin(). Reads only the volume header, so it returns at once.

    • freeKiB

      int freeKiB()
      The card volume's free space in KiB, or -1 before a successful begin(). A FAT32 card's own free-space count (its FSInfo sector, kept by the computer that last wrote the card) answers at once, though it may lag a few clusters behind writes the board made since. Without one, the whole allocation table is counted, which can take a minute on a large card; the count pauses between slices so other threads keep running, but the calling thread waits for all of it, so call this from a background thread and keep the result.
